title: Regular locus is open when every prime quotient has a regular open
statement: Let $A$ be a commutative Noetherian ring [def-weil-pbc-noetherian-ring]. Suppose that for every prime ideal $\mathfrak p\subset A$, the spectrum $\operatorname{Spec}(A/\mathfrak p)$ [def-weil-affine-spectrum] contains a nonempty open subset $U_{\mathfrak p}$ such that $(A/\mathfrak p)_{\mathfrak q}$ [def-weil-pbc-localization-at-prime] is regular local [def-weil-regular-scheme] for every $\mathfrak q\in U_{\mathfrak p}$. Then $\{\mathfrak q\in\operatorname{Spec}A:A_{\mathfrak q}\text{ is regular local}\}$ is open in $\operatorname{Spec}A$.

source.place: Tag 07P9, lemma-intersection-regular-with-closed; J-0 and J-1 expanded using Tag 07P7, definition-J.

proof.text: Write $E=\{\mathfrak p:A_{\mathfrak p}\text{ is regular local}\}$. This property is stable under passing to smaller primes. Indeed, if $\mathfrak q\subseteq\mathfrak p$ and $\mathfrak p\in E$, [lem-weil-pbc-primes-of-localization] gives the prime $Q=\mathfrak qA_{\mathfrak p}$ of $A_{\mathfrak p}$. Its localization is regular local by [lem-weil-pbc-regular-local-localization], and [lem-weil-pbc-localize-localization-at-prime] identifies it with $A_{\mathfrak q}$. This proves hypothesis (i) of the criterion to be used in step 7.

source.place: Tag 07P9 via Tag 07P8, lemma-J-1: generalization stability; algebra.tex Tag 0AFS.

proof.text: Fix a prime $\mathfrak p\in E$. By the definition of regular local [def-weil-regular-scheme], its maximal ideal $\mathfrak pA_{\mathfrak p}$ admits $r=\dim A_{\mathfrak p}$ generators. Represent them by fractions $a_i/s_i$, with $a_i\in\mathfrak p$ and $s_i\notin\mathfrak p$, using [def-weil-pbc-localization-at-prime]. Since each $s_i/1$ is a unit, $f_i=a_i$ have images $f_i/1$ generating the same maximal ideal. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-regular-local-generators-regular-sequence] to these $r$ generators: their images form a regular sequence in $A_{\mathfrak p}$. This includes $r=0$.

source.place: Tag 07P9, first three sentences; algebra.tex Tag 00NQ.

proof.text: Apply [lem-exc-regular-sequence-principal-neighbourhood] to $A$, $\mathfrak p$ and the sequence $f_i$. Obtain $g\notin\mathfrak p$ such that the images of the $f_i$ form a regular sequence in $A_g$.

We now make the same $f_i$ generate $\mathfrak p$ on a smaller neighbourhood, spelling out the second replacement in the source. The map $A_g	o B$ is localization at the image of $\prod_js_j$: its fractions are obtained by inverting this product. By [lem-weil-pbc-localization-module-exact], localization preserves the injective multiplication maps on each successive quotient that define the regular sequence in step 3. Put $C=A_g$, $s=\prod_js_j$ (viewed in $C$), and $J_i=(f_1,\ldots,f_{i-1})C$. The identification $(C/J_i)[1/s]\cong B/J_iB$ sends $(c+J_i)/s^n$ to $c/s^n+J_iB$. It is surjective because every element of $B$ is $c/s^n$; its kernel is zero because $c/s^n\in J_iB$ exactly when $s^Nc\in J_i$ for some $N$, exactly the criterion that $(c+J_i)/s^n=0$. Conversely $s^Nc\in J_i$ gives the ideal membership after inverting $s$. This map commutes with multiplication by every $f_i$ by its displayed formula. otin\mathfrak p$. Hence the $f_i$ are a regular sequence in $B$ by [def-weil-pbc-regular-sequence].

proof.text: Fix such a prime $\mathfrak q$. In $B=A_h$ the prime $Q=\{a/h^n:a\in\mathfrak q\}$ contains every image of $f_i$, and $B_Q\cong A_{\mathfrak q}$. Concretely the isomorphism sends $(a/h^n)/(c/h^m)$ to $ah^m/(ch^n)$, where $c\notin\mathfrak q$; its inverse sends $a/s$ to $(a/1)/(s/1)$, and cross multiplication checks the two inverses. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-weakly-regular-sequence-localization-prime] to the regular sequence of step 4 and $Q$. It gives a regular sequence $f_i/1$ in $A_{\mathfrak q}$. The equality $\mathfrak pB=IB$ implies $\mathfrak pA_{\mathfrak q}=(f_i)A_{\mathfrak q}$. By [lem-weil-pbc-localization-at-prime-of-quotient], its quotient is isomorphic to $(A/\mathfrak p)_{\bar{\mathfrak q}}$, regular by step 5. The local ring $A_{\mathfrak q}$ is Noetherian by [lem-weil-pbc-localization-noetherian]. Apply [lem-exc-regular-local-lift-regular-sequence-quotient] to conclude $A_{\mathfrak q}$ is regular local. Thus the element $k$ constructed in step 5 verifies hypothesis (ii) of the criterion for this $\mathfrak p$.

proof.text: Apply [lem-exc-nagata-principal-open-criterion] to the predicate on ideals which means that the ideal is prime and its localization is regular local (assign it false on nonprime ideals). Step 1 gives hypothesis (i) and steps 2-6 give hypothesis (ii). Therefore every $\mathfrak p\in E$ belongs to some principal open $D(t)\subseteq E$. Principal opens are open directly from the closed-set description in [lem-weil-pbc-spec-irreducible-closed-subsets-primes], since $D(t)=\operatorname{Spec}A\setminus V((t))$. Their union is exactly $E$, so $E$ is open. For the zero ring the spectrum and this union are empty; no regular prime was chosen.
